title: Cover Picture and Issue Information
content:
A female American alligator guards her nest. Within the nest, developing embryos respond to temperature fluctuations, which will determine if they develop as males or females. (Credit: Benjamin Parrott).

This month's cover image is provided by the authors of ‘An epigenomic threshold hypothesis for integrating dynamic environmental signals into functional models of developmental polyphenisms’ (https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2435.70099). The article, which develops an epigenomic threshold hypothesis for integrating ecologically and biologically relevant timescales into a mechanistic model, is part of the ‘Causes and Consequences of Phenotypic Plasticity’ Special Feature published in this issue. The feature identifies new and exciting research themes on the eco-evolutionary causes and consequences of phenotypic plasticity and synthesizes our understanding of phenotypic plasticity and its functional ecology.
